results.ask: What's special about my block? I'm on 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega.
results.expect: calls about_block; gives the block's own figures and something pinned nearby, with sources; cites
results.answer:
Your block sits about 39 feet above sea level, and its homes were typically built around 1941. Two model homes from World War II stood a few blocks east: the Rainbow House (1941) and the Freedom House (1942) on 42nd and 43rd Avenues between Moraga and Noriega.

Old photographs are pinned at 46th and Moraga and at 45th and Noriega; open them to see the street in years past.

Street cleaning:
- East side: Mondays 1st & 3rd, noon–2pm (next: Nov 16)
- West side: Thursdays 1st, 3rd, 5th, noon–2pm (next: Nov 19)

The city's signs on the block are the last word.

A neighbor who lived here since the 1970s could tell you more about how the block has changed.

- West side: Thursdays on the 1st, 3rd, and 5th, noon to 2pm (next: November 19).

The city's signs on the block are the last word. [SF Public Works](https://sfpublicworks.org/services/mechanical-street-sweeping-and-street-cleaning-schedule)

results.expect: uses the block the neighbor shared without asking for cross streets; cites
results.answer:
Your block sits about 39 feet above sea level on dune sand, with homes built around 1941. Right near here, at 43rd and Moraga, Doelger built Freedom House and Rainbow House in 1941–42 as patriotic model homes before wartime halted new construction. The King Philip clipper ship lies buried under the sand near Noriega and Ortega, surfacing after big winter storms.

Old photographs are pinned at 46th and Moraga and 45th and Noriega [OpenSFHistory](https://opensfhistory.org).
